title: AID Test Portfolio — Execution Unit Receipt
$comment: producer: scripts/lib/aid-test-execution-unit.sh (execution_unit_receipt); consumer: any caller aggregating per-unit results. P078 removed the scheduler producer and its report merge with the parallelism machinery; the shape is unchanged.
description: Deterministic report shape for a scheduled batch of execution units (Step 1's shape) and their terminal/non-terminal outcomes. Sort key for `units[]` is ALWAYS unit_id — never arrival or completion order — so two batches built from the same units in a different execution order serialize to byte-identical output.

unit_id.description: MUST equal the execution unit's own unit_id (Step 1) — never a separately-derived identity.

job_id.description: The aid-job.sh job id this unit was dispatched under.

state.description: aid-job.sh's own state vocabulary (via aid-test-execution-unit.sh's status/receipt normalization, Step 1) — never a second, competing vocabulary. started/running/lost are non-terminal; the rest are terminal.

duration_ms.description: null while non-terminal — never fabricated from a partial run. Whole-second-quantized (see aid-test-execution-unit.sh's own documented limitation).

concurrency_context.description: Always "sequential" since P078 removed parallel execution; kept so historical receipts and the baseline series keep a stable field.

co_scheduled_with.description: Always empty since P078 removed parallel execution: nothing is ever co-scheduled. Kept (rather than dropped) so historical receipts stay readable; constrained to empty so a receipt can never claim concurrent peers while declaring concurrency_context: sequential.

stdout_path.description: Path to the unit's streamed stdout log (aid-job.sh's own stdout_path).

allOf.$comment: Non-terminal states never carry a fabricated duration/exit_code — matches aid-test-execution-unit.sh's execution_unit_receipt, which emits both as null for every non-terminal state.
aid-job.sh's normal cmd_wrap completion path always records ended_epoch for these three states, so duration_ms/exit_code are always present — the null exception below is cancelled-only.

aid-job.sh's cancel path always sets exit_code:143 (even the pre-exec-handshake _wrap_write_cancelled_result), but duration_ms may legitimately be null — that handshake result carries no ended_epoch at all since the command never ran.

units.description: Sorted by unit_id (ascending, byte/codepoint order) at serialization time — the canonical, deterministic ordering every producer/consumer of this shape agrees on.
